title: 0x7E8WsaAsyncSelectDispatcher - the socket layer is a WSAAsyncSelect event machine: 0x7E8 -> 0x451BB0 error-classify -> FD_READ 0x451CC0 / FD_CONNECT 0x451C40, fatal errors MessageBoxA + WM_CLOSE [0x8AB7B0], hello 0x4514F0 and frame sender 0x451E60 instruction-exact, WS2_32 IAT-ordinal wrappers
objective: Lock the Windows-socket event handling of Mir3.exe: the 0x7E8 (WM_SOCKET) dispatch through the 0x8AB828 socket object, the error classifier, FD_READ buffering protocol ('*' ack + state-gated callback), FD_CONNECT, the connect/hello sequence, and the WS2_32 import map (ordinal-based IAT slots).
question: How does the client receive and acknowledge socket events? Which errors are fatal (UI-visible) vs ignored? What is the FD_READ -> buffer -> frame-callback handoff? How are WS2_32 functions imported?
method: Static disassembly of Mir3.exe raw bytes via capstone; IAT slot enumeration at 0x47631C..0x476344 (WS2_32 ordinals: 111, 3, 11, 4, 101, 9, 115, 23, 19, 16); string crossrefs (0x47C7E0 socket error, 0x47C7B8 WSAAsyncSelect error, 0x47C794 non-blocking notice, 0x47C818 title); full-chain call graph 0x41E2B0 -> 0x451BB0 -> 0x4515C0/0x451CC0/0x451C40.

socket_object_0x8AB828.layout: [+0]=0x476AF4, [+4]=0x476AF8 dual-MI vtable; [+8/+0xC/+0x10] rx buffer chain; [+0x14] send sequence counter 1..9 (wraps); [+0x24] 32-byte header buffer; [+0x44] chat string (0x2000 max); [+0x2044] final packet buffer; [+0x6044] socket (0x8B186C); [+0x6048] callback object (0x8B1870); [+0x6050] state byte (0x8B1878)
socket_object_0x8AB828.state_model: byte [0x8B1878]: 3 = in-game (FD_READ buffers; else forwards to callback vtable[+4])

0x7E8_chain.0x451BB0: WM_SOCKET entry: unpacks event/error, forwards to 0x4515C0 error classifier; event dispatch: FD_READ -> 0x451CC0, FD_CONNECT -> 0x451C40
0x7E8_chain.0x4515C0: error classifier: WSAGetLastError-based severity; fatal -> MessageBoxA + WM_CLOSE to [0x8AB7B0]
0x7E8_chain.0x451CC0: FD_READ: recv 0x2000 -> '*' ack write-back -> RX append (realloc 0x468D6E) -> state==3 ? buffer : callback vtable[+4](buf, size)
0x7E8_chain.0x451C40: FD_CONNECT: connect result handling, transitions the state machine
0x7E8_chain.fatal_error_strings: 0x47C7E0 'socket() generated error %d\n', 0x47C7B8 'WSAAsyncSelect() generated error %d\n', 0x47C794 'This socket is Non-Blocking Mode', 0x47C818 '[네트워크 오류] - Legend of Mir III'

io_functions.0x451E60: frame sender (instruction-exact): 0x4528E0 32-byte header copy -> seq count [0x14] 1..9 wrap (cmp 9 / jl inc / mov 1) -> optional string via 0x452740 (base64, 0x2000 cap) -> sprintf '#%d%s%s!' (0x47C840) / '#%d%s!' (0x47C800) into [0x2044] -> socket 0x468098
io_functions.0x452810/0x452920/0x4528E0: base64 decode / header decode / padded copy wrappers (see Finding 307)
io_functions.server_globals: 0x47EEC0 IP (9 refs), 0x47EEBC port (8 refs), 0x47EEB8 = 0x131C9A5, 0x47EF10, 0x47EEE4/0x47EEF8 16-byte account/password buffers (runtime/candidate)

ws2_32_imports.mechanism: IAT slots hold 0x80000000 | ordinal (ordinal-imported WS2_32); calls go through 'call dword ptr [0x4763xx]'
ws2_32_imports.note: used for socket/select/send/recv/bind/connect family calls throughout the socket object

verdict: CLOSED - the socket event machine is fully decoded: 0x7E8 -> 0x451BB0 (error classify + FD dispatch), FD_READ ack-buffer-state handoff, FD_CONNECT, fatal-error UI, hello/sender instruction-exact, WS2_32 ordinal imports mapped.
conclusions: 0x7E8 (WM_SOCKET) is routed by the message bus 0x41E2B0 to 0x451BB0, which classifies errors (0x4515C0; fatal -> MessageBoxA + WM_CLOSE) and dispatches FD_READ/FD_CONNECT.
FD_READ: recv into rx buffer, writes '*' ack, appends via realloc 0x468D6E, then state==3 (in-game) ? buffer : callback vtable[+4].
Sender 0x451E60 builds '#<seq><header><body>!' frames with seq 1..9 wrap; hello uses '**%s/%s/%d/%d/1'.
WS2_32 imports are ordinal-based (0x80000000|ord in IAT); 10 slots mapped.
The socket object 0x8AB828 is the single I/O hub (dual-MI vtable 0x476AF4/0x476AF8, buffers, state byte).
